intro.title: Quick tour of PodoType
intro.body: A few short steps — where services show up, what the health summary means, how to tell if tracing itself is working, and where to drill into a slow request. Skip any time.

services.title: Services, found automatically
services.body: Every container running on this host shows up here on its own — no SDK, no per-service config, no code changes. Watch the ones you care about from this list.

overview.title: What's healthy, at a glance
overview.body: This reads back as a plain sentence: how many watched services are up, and whether anything's actively breaching an alert threshold right now.

preflight.title: If tracing itself isn't working
preflight.body: Zero-code tracing relies on the host kernel supporting eBPF. If that's missing or beyla fails to start, this exact spot names the problem instead of just showing empty charts.

traces.title: Drill into a slow request
traces.body: Once a service is reporting, Traces is where you see the actual call path and where time was spent — click into any trace for the full waterfall.

selectServices.title: Select services to track
selectServices.intro: Every container on this host, read straight from the Docker API — no traffic required. Toggle the ones you want to watch, then continue — you can always come back to add more later.
selectServices.manualAddPlaceholder: Service name (for something not running as a container on this host)

discoveredTable.noContainers: No containers found — check that /var/run/docker.sock is mounted into PodoType's app container (see docker-compose.yml).

watchedRow.slowestTitle: Highest trace p95 latency among your watched services right now
watchedRow.clearDataTitle: Delete this service's own stored spans, logs and metrics history

criticalPath.title: Critical path
criticalPath.footnote: The chain of calls still running when this request finally finished — not every span that ran, just the ones on the hook for the total time.

alertsPanel.title: Alerts
alertsPanel.deliveryTooltip: Sustained for {{checks}} consecutive checks before firing. Delivery: {{channels}}.
alertsPanel.deliveryTooltipSimple: Sustained for {{checks}} consecutive checks before firing.

alertsSettings.triggersTooltip: Each of these already computes a live status elsewhere on this dashboard — this just decides whether that status is also allowed to fire a sustained alert.
alertsSettings.serviceDownHint: a watched container reports not running/unhealthy
alertsSettings.storageHint: ClickHouse's own volume is running low
alertsSettings.errorRateHint: a watched service's real request traffic is coming back 5xx
alertsSettings.latencyHint: p95 response time crosses the line below
alertsSettings.thresholdNote: Error rate and latency only ever fire for a service that Beyla is already seeing real traffic for — switch them on once you've confirmed that under eBPF Data.
alertsSettings.sustainedTooltip: A condition has to stay breached across this many consecutive checks (checked every 15s) before it actually fires, and clears the moment one check comes back healthy — avoids alerting on a single noisy blip.
alertsSettings.telegramDesc: Free — message a bot you create via @BotFather, then send it any message once so it can find your chat ID.
alertsSettings.webhookDesc: Works with Slack, Discord, or anything else that accepts an incoming webhook URL.
alertsSettings.emailDesc: Sent via your own mailbox — Gmail, Google Workspace, Zoho Mail, Outlook, or any other SMTP provider. Use an app-specific password if your provider asks for one once 2FA is on (Gmail/Workspace: myaccount.google.com/apppasswords; Zoho: Security › App Passwords).

hostedAlertsSettings.triggersTooltip: Evaluated centrally, not by the agent — a crashed customer VM shouldn't take its own alerting down with it. Checked every ~30s.
hostedAlertsSettings.serviceDownHint: a watched container reports not running/unhealthy
hostedAlertsSettings.errorRateHint: a watched service's traced error rate crosses the threshold below
hostedAlertsSettings.noChannelsYet: No channels yet — add one below.

serviceAlertOverrides.memoryAbsNote: requires the "Memory threshold" trigger to also be on — no global default; this is the one to use for a plain "alert if this service uses more than N MB" rule.

hostStats.tooltip: CPU, memory, load average and uptime for the whole machine this runs on — not any one container. Read directly from the host's /proc, no extra containers or agents involved.
hostStats.pointInTimeOnly: Point-in-time only — hosted doesn't store host-level history yet, so this always shows the current reading regardless of the selected time range.
hostStats.retentionNote: Only the last ~{{minutes}}m of host history is kept — showing all of it, not the full selected range.
hostStats.notAvailable: Host metrics aren't available yet — still gathering the first sample.

resourceHealth.title: Container health
resourceHealth.tooltip: CPU, memory, network and disk I/O for this container itself, read directly from Docker (the same numbers `docker stats` shows), plus request/error rate history where Beyla has resolved this container to a service. Separate from request-level tracing above. Memory shows a percent-of-limit only if this container's compose entry actually sets a memory limit.

possibleCause.title: Possible cause
possibleCause.footnote: Based on one recent trace ({{traceId}}…) — a possible explanation, not a confirmed diagnosis.

rootCause.title: Likely origin
rootCause.degradedFirst_one: degraded first{{ago}} — {{count}} other service ({{others}}) started breaching after. This is based on alert timing, not a confirmed cause — worth checking {{service}} first.
rootCause.degradedFirst_other: degraded first{{ago}} — {{count}} other services ({{others}}) started breaching after. This is based on alert timing, not a confirmed cause — worth checking {{service}} first.

retentionPanel.recentVolume_one: Recent volume: ~{{bytes}}/day (based on the last {{count}} full day).
retentionPanel.recentVolume_other: Recent volume: ~{{bytes}}/day (based on the last {{count}} full days).
retentionPanel.atThatRate: At that rate, {{daysPhrase}} of retention would use approximately {{bytes}}.
retentionPanel.noVolumeEstimate: No volume estimate available yet{{errSuffix}} — a new deployment needs at least a little trace data before this can estimate anything.
retentionPanel.longerRetentionTooltip: Longer retention keeps more history for post-hoc debugging and (later) baselining, but uses more of ClickHouse's own disk. There's no hard limit here — pick whatever you actually want; just keep an eye on the Disk space status if you're already close to full.
retentionPanel.reclaimTooltip: Without this, shortening retention only changes the cutoff going forward — old rows still age out on ClickHouse's own background schedule, which can take a while. Checking this forces ClickHouse to rewrite its data and drop expired rows right now instead (real disk I/O — may take a bit on a large table).
retentionPanel.enterDaysError: Enter a number of days greater than 0.

logRetentionPanel.recentVolume_one: Recent volume: ~{{bytes}}/day (based on the last {{count}} full day) across every service with log storage turned on.
logRetentionPanel.recentVolume_other: Recent volume: ~{{bytes}}/day (based on the last {{count}} full days) across every service with log storage turned on.
logRetentionPanel.noVolumeEstimate: No volume estimate yet — this fills in once at least one service has log storage enabled (see any service's Logs → History tab) and has been running long enough to have a full day of data.
logRetentionPanel.tooltip: This bounds how long STORED log patterns are kept — a separate setting from trace retention above, and from whatever Docker's own log driver does with its own copy of your logs. Shortening this doesn't reduce Docker's own log disk usage at all.
logRetentionPanel.separateNote: Separate from trace retention — this only affects services with log storage turned on.
logRetentionPanel.reclaimTooltip: Without this, shortening retention only changes the cutoff going forward — old rows still age out on ClickHouse's own background schedule, which can take a while. Checking this forces ClickHouse to rewrite its data and drop expired rows right now instead.

logsPanel.title: Logs
logsPanel.tooltip: Live tail of this container's own stdout/stderr, unfiltered — new lines appear as they're written, the same as `docker logs -f` or Grafana's Live view. Clustered groups a larger recent tail into recurring line shapes instead, so a noisy repeating message doesn't bury anything different. Only fetches/streams while this section is open.
logsPanel.tabHistoryTooltip: Stored pattern history — opt-in, see the History tab itself for the trade-off
logsPanel.clusterSummary_one: {{count}} distinct pattern across the last {{lines}} lines
logsPanel.clusterSummary_other: {{count}} distinct patterns across the last {{lines}} lines
logsPanel.offDesc: Off by default. This tab reads from Docker's live logs directly, same as Live/Clustered — nothing about PodoType stores log data anywhere. Turning this on for {{service}} starts a SECOND, small copy — clustered patterns, not raw lines — kept independently in ClickHouse so history survives a restart and time-range search actually means something. This is genuinely additional disk usage on top of whatever Docker's own logs already use, not a replacement for them or a way to reduce it.
logsPanel.shorterRetention: Showing the last {{hoursUsed}}h — that's your current log retention, shorter than the {{hoursRequested}}h range you picked.
logsPanel.noStoredPatterns: no stored patterns in this window yet
logsPanel.diskCriticalWarning: Disk space is critical — Docker can't persist new log lines right now, so this may look frozen even though the stream itself is connected. Not a bug here; see the Disk space banner above.
logsPanel.searchOlderTooltip: This box only filters what's already arrived since you opened this tab — search a bigger recent history on the container itself instead
logsPanel.noMatchInBuffer: no lines in the current buffer match "{{query}}"

usageStats.vcpuRamRef: {{cores}} vCPU · {{ram}} RAM — reference price for a similarly-sized VPS, not your actual bill
usageStats.spansInRangeSub: across everything stored in the last {{range}}
usageStats.ingestRateSub: averaged over the last {{range}} — pick a wider range above to smooth out short bursts/lulls
usageStats.ingestRateInfo: This is SPANS per second, not requests — one traced request usually produces more than one span (the request itself, plus any downstream/DB/internal calls Beyla captured alongside it), so this number naturally runs higher than your requests/sec. It's also an average over whichever range is selected above, not a live instant reading — if traffic was heavier earlier in a longer window than it is right now, the cumulative 'Spans this month' total can grow faster than this rate alone would suggest. Widen the range to see a more representative average.
usageStats.overCapMsg: Over the free-tier cap — new spans are being dropped until next month.

serviceDependencies.noRelationships: No call relationships seen for this service in the last {{minutes}} minutes — either nothing calls it (or it calls nothing) yet, or there's not enough trace data.

serviceMap.noTraffic: No traced traffic in the last {{minutes}} minutes yet — the map fills in once Beyla or an OTel agent has captured some real requests.
serviceMap.whoCallsWhom: Who calls whom — last {{minutes}}m of real traffic
serviceMap.tooltip: On self-hosted, an arrow is backed by Beyla's real observed TCP connections (network-flow eBPF capture) whenever one's available this window — that's what a solid line means; trace correlation alone (matching a caller's outbound span to a callee's inbound span by trace ID) fills in call counts and p95 latency, and supplies the edge on its own — shown dashed — when no confirming connection was seen this round. Hosted now confirms edges the same way — real TCP connections its agent observes, forwarded up and matched here. Node names are Beyla's (or an OTel agent's) own service names, which don't always match PodoType's watched-container names — see the dashboard's own 'Beyla name resolution' for why. A service with no callers/callees shown either hasn't made or received a traced request in this window, or only ever gets health-check traffic.
serviceMap.titleUnconfirmed: — from trace data only, no live TCP connection observed this window
serviceMap.titleConfirmed: — confirmed by a real TCP connection

serviceDetailPage.notWatchedAnymore: That service isn't watched anymore — it may have just been removed or stopped.

serviceSloPanel.noConditions: No SLO conditions configured yet for this service — set an error-rate{{suffix}} threshold above to get one.

compareServices.noServicesYet: No watched services yet — add some from the Services page first.
compareServices.pickAtLeastOne: Pick at least one service above to compare.

beylaPanel.title: eBPF (Beyla)
beylaPanel.tooltip: Runs automatically for every container, no setup here — a shared host-wide watcher (see docker-compose.yml) captures RED metrics and real OTLP spans with nothing installed inside any of your services. Spans are shallower (process-boundary, not code-level) than the OTel agent's, and it needs a real Linux kernel with eBPF/BTF support — it won't do much on stock Docker Desktop. This panel goes quiet whenever there's been no traffic in the last few minutes, or when the OTel agent below is also enabled and showing its own (deeper) data instead — neither means this stopped working.
beylaPanel.agentShowing: This service's own OpenTelemetry agent is enabled and reporting — see the Tracing panel for its spans. eBPF keeps watching in the background either way, nothing to configure here.
beylaPanel.noSpansYet: No spans in the last few minutes — normal if this service has been quiet. Nothing to configure; this appears on its own the moment traffic hits it.

billingPanel.cappedDesc: Capped at 10 watched services, 15 days retention.
billingPanel.freeTierTooltip: Free tier applies whenever this install isn't currently subscribed — including before the first Subscribe click, or if a payment lapses for more than 48 hours (or the license server is unreachable for more than 5 days). Nothing already running is deleted; watching an 11th service is what gets blocked until you subscribe or free one up.
billingPanel.unlimitedDesc: Unlimited watched services, full retention control.
billingPanel.upgradingNotAvailable: Upgrading isn't available yet — check back soon.
billingPanel.paddleLoadError: Could not load Paddle checkout — try again in a moment.

bulkOtelSetup.description: Check the services to trace, pick each one's language, then generate one merged config covering all of them. Unchecking an already-traced service here turns tracing off for it.
bulkOtelSetup.noWatchedServices: No watched services yet — watch some first, then come back here.
bulkOtelSetup.noLanguagesSupported: No OTel languages supported by this build yet.

otelInstructions.copyFailedAlert: Could not copy automatically — select the text below and copy it manually.
otelInstructions.closeTitleDefault: Close (tracing stays enabled — this just hides these instructions; reopen from the instructions link)
otelInstructions.cleanupLabel: 2. Clean up leftover fetch containers (after the traced set changes — safe, only matches podotype's own; do NOT use --remove-orphans here, see below)
otelInstructions.ciCdRecommended: Recommended for CI/CD — paste at the top of the real docker-compose.yml your pipeline deploys, so this override applies automatically on every rebuild (needs Compose v2.20+)

profilingPanel.description: Continuous CPU profiling via Parca Agent (eBPF, zero code changes) — profiles every process on the host all the time, so "where did the CPU go" has an answer even without an incident to trigger it.
profilingPanel.newNote: This is new and not yet verified end-to-end on a real host — see docker-compose.yml's profiler/profiler-agent services. Parca ships its own flamegraph UI rather than this app building a second one.

traceExplorer.hiddenHealthChecks_other: {{count}} health-check traces hidden (/actuator/health & similar) so real requests aren't crowded out

traceLogsPanel.title: Logs during this trace
traceLogsPanel.noLogsFound: no logs found in this trace's window
traceLogsPanel.noMatchingLines: no matching log lines in this trace's time window

traceWaterfall.noAttributes: No span attributes recorded for this one.
traceWaterfall.noSpanData: No span data for this trace.
traceWaterfall.singleSpanTrace: Single-span trace — nothing to compare against. This usually means a background call with no downstream calls of its own (e.g. a connection-pool keepalive), not a full request: {{service}} · {{operation}} · {{duration}}ms.
traceWaterfall.clickHint: · click a span for its attributes
traceWaterfall.legendSlowest: red bar = the single slowest span in this trace, or one that returned an error — that's usually where to start looking.
traceWaterfall.legendCrossService: Highlighted service names mark where the call crossed into another service.

tracesPanel.title: Traces
tracesPanel.tooltip: Two independent ways this service's requests can show up here: Spans (automatic, always on, no setup — a shared host-wide watcher captures shallower process-boundary spans for every container) and Code Tracing (opt-in, needs a small compose-file addition, deeper code-level spans via a real OpenTelemetry agent). Whichever one actually has data for this service shows its trace list below.
tracesPanel.requestsChartInfo: Every request Beyla's eBPF watcher saw for this container, charted over time.
tracesPanel.errorRateChartInfo: Share of requests that came back with a 5xx status, charted over time.
tracesPanel.latencyChartInfo: The full latency distribution, not just one percentile — p99 shows the tail a p95-only chart can hide.
tracesPanel.noDataYet: no data in the last few minutes yet
tracesPanel.requestsRowInfo: Every request Beyla's eBPF watcher saw for this container, counted directly — not limited to the handful of traces shown below. Rate is requests/sec over the last ~15s; errors are the share of those with a 5xx status.
tracesPanel.noTelemetryStored: no telemetry stored in the last minute
tracesPanel.ingestionRowInfo: How much telemetry is actually being stored for this service right now, separate from request rate above — spans/sec written to the trace store, and logs/sec written to the log store (only counted when this service has log storage turned on).
tracesPanel.quietCodeTracingLive: quiet — Code Tracing below is live instead
tracesPanel.offManageSidebar: off — manage from Code Tracing in the sidebar
tracesPanel.enabledWaiting: enabled — waiting for its first spans
tracesPanel.notAvailableHosted: not available for hosted deployments yet — Spans above already cover this service automatically

tracingPanel.title: Tracing
tracingPanel.tooltip: Real cross-service trace waterfalls, via an OpenTelemetry agent. Not zero-touch: needs one shared compose file applied alongside your main one (PodoType generates and keeps it up to date — covers every traced service, not just this one). Supported languages: {{languages}}.
tracingPanel.offSuffix: for full code-level spans (eBPF already covers this service automatically — see the eBPF panel below).
tracingPanel.waitingFirstSpans: Enabled — waiting for its first spans from this service's own OpenTelemetry agent. This can take a minute after first applying the setup file, or after a restart.
tracingPanel.setupFileTooltip: This service is set up as {{language}} — opens the one shared setup file covering every traced service, not just this one

chartPanel.emptyDefault: No data yet for this window.

fleetGoldenSignals.fleetRequestsInfo: Every watched service's own request rate, stacked — the stack height at any point is the fleet total.
fleetGoldenSignals.noTrafficYet: No request traffic observed yet across watched services.
fleetGoldenSignals.fleetErrorRateInfo: Request-weighted average error rate across every watched service.
fleetGoldenSignals.p95LatencyInfo: Each watched service's own p95 latency — which one is actually dragging, not just a single worst-case number.
fleetGoldenSignals.noTraceDataYet: No trace data yet across watched services.
